description.name: merge_tables
description.description: Combines up to 20 CSVs into a single table. Headers do not have to match: columns are unioned and a file missing a column contributes blanks for it, so rows never shift silently — the failure mode that makes hand-merged spreadsheets untrustworthy. description.name: reconcile_ledger
description.description: Reconciles two sets of records — your books against a bank, platform, or supplier statement. Matches rows on a key column, compares an amount column, and returns three lists: only in A, only in B, and same key but different amount. description.name: fix_csv_encoding
description.description: Detect the real encoding of a CSV (GB18030, Shift-JIS, Windows-1252…), repair mojibake (UTF-8 that was read as Latin-1, e.g. "Ã©"), and re-emit UTF-8 with a BOM so Excel opens it correctly.

description.name: read_xlsx
description.description: Read an Excel .xlsx workbook (by URL) into rows — every sheet, or one you name. Returns cell values (not formula text), dates as YYYY-MM-DD instead of Excel serial numbers, and keeps leading zeros so ID/postcode columns are not silently mangled. Says plainly which sheet it used, which sheets are hid

description.name: write_xlsx
description.description: Build an Excel .xlsx file from rows (CSV text or JSON arrays), optionally several sheets at once. Numbers are written as real numbers so they sum in Excel, while values with leading zeros stay text so IDs and postcodes survive the round trip.

description.name: match_transactions
description.description: Match bank statement lines to ledger/invoice entries when there is NO shared key — by amount, date window, reference numbers found inside free-text descriptions, and fuzzy counterparty names ("北京XX科技" vs "XX科技(北京)"). Handles split payments (one invoice paid in instalments, 1:N) and combined payments

description.name: dedupe_entities

description.name: csv_to_chart
